tweets.text:
Morgan Stanley’s 2027 outlook goes “max overweight” global stocks, saying “With risk assets having cheapened, we embrace risk.” It added to equities in every region:

▪️ U.S. stays overweight; Japan and Europe raised to overweight; EM stays equal weight.
▪️ End-2027 targets: S&P 500 8,700 (+15%), TOPIX 4,800 (+22%), MSCI Europe 3,030 (+15%), MSCI EM 1,760 (+13%).
▪️ Funded by cutting the rest of fixed income, commodities and cash; corporate credit raised to equal weight; likes gold.
▪️ Expects $1.7T of hyperscaler capex in 2027 and $1.8T in 2028, and says AI is broadening to adopters.

Wilson’s new 8,700 target (from 8,000) is 19x his 2028 EPS of $458. His EPS path is $369 / $420 / $458 for 2026–28 (+34% / +14% / +9%).

So the whole target raise has come from earnings. Since May Wilson has lifted his 2027 EPS 11% while cutting the multiple to 19x from about 20.5x. Notably his 14% 2027 growth is still below the 16.2% analysts expect (FactSet).

Note also the bank is calling for the 10-year Treasury rate to fall to 5.05% in 1H27 even with two more Fed rate hikes. The S&P’s forward earnings yield (18.3x per FactSet) is about 5.5%, only about a third of a point over the current 5.14% 10-year. On trailing earnings, stocks now yield 1.31 points less than the 10-year, the widest gap since 2009. 

With Goldman and Barclays also at 8,700 for next year, the debate is whether the earnings show up. Wilson also says says a retest of 7,100–7,300 “could still lie ahead.”

“Our view dating back to late September has been that the correction associated with the mid cycle transition would conclude with the S&P 500 catching down to narrow breadth. That process is now well advanced as the index has approached our established 7,100–7,300 support range,” he said. “While a retest could still lie ahead, the recent correction provides the springboard for the next leg higher toward our new 8,700 base case.”

As long as the market is good and a consistent spicket of copy traders are there, they do fine.

When the market dries up and the copy traders disappear, they turn to gambling purely lower mcap coins and trading w/ high leverage and slowly bleed their ports dry.

Majority of them (and their followers) would outperform by simply stacking and concentrating capital in high conviction plays and waiting for the market to turn around and do the work for them.

The average repurchase price of $STRC was $99.93 per share. Practically no discount, and zero new issuance on a week when it touched $100.

Yes.

Also yes.

They have plenty of cash on hand to cover the convertibles due over the next couple of years, which are very likely also going to have be repurchased... especially considering the MSCI news recently.

This summer we knew they had to pick a sacrificial lamb to heal -

the options were either Bitcoin, STRC holders, or MSTR shareholders.

They chose MSTR.

Reminder:

If you're bullish on Bitcoin, just buy Bitcoin.

A little more colour:

The extent of the recent fall has been severe, but that itself does not mean much if what is happening is a rapid repricing of tightening liquidity conditions

We have many competing forces now: strong historical support levels, 5-year CAGR approaching 2022 bottom, 11-day streak of lower highs (an all-time record today at 12 if we hold below yesterday's high), mass long liquidations, OI dominance reset etc.

But concurrently we have rapidly tightening dollar liquidity and a strong negative trend, with many, many more long liquidations piled up below

Think the most probable scenario is near-term relief here purely based on how many consecutive lower highs we've put in followed by continuation lower later this month - and that next move lower is likely where everyone entirely gives up on BTC 

Given I have now roundtripped my spot pos. back to entry I will look to buy my own blood if/when we get capitulation below 62 as I do not think this is the beginning of a secular bear + 5-year CAGR is at its most attractive from a contrarian POV + expect tightening liquidity conditions to be temporary not structural into 2027

However, the outlook for the next 13w is now pretty bleak despite the severity of the recent decline - in historical cases, despite a prior 14-day 10%+ decline, the median 13w return has been -8%, with 40% hit rate and negative skew on MFE/MAE. My systematic strategy remains flat and the BTC liquidity model I built recently also flipped to cash on Friday close (though this is not a live model unlike the systematic, just something I have been tinkering with recently)

My indicators are also approaching the buy zone again but not flashing 'BUY' yet like they did in Feb and July

Before buying my own blood, I'd want to see some combination of exhaustion in negative liquidity momentum (ROC peaks and turns) + more long liqs and persistent fear to buy the dip on perps unlike now + my systematic and/or liquidity model flipping to BUY

My own discretionary decision-making came at own detriment from a near-perfect entry to what should have been a very good exit - we all have those trades (and will continue to do so) but particularly frustrating when my own systems tell me something and I ignore thinking my discretionary view is smarter 🙃

As cheap as it has ever been relative to its own trend but with massive headwinds currently weighing it down 

Historically, when we have traded to valuation extremes in tightening conditions, the fwd returns have been less attractive near-term - and as you might imagine when these valuation extremes occur in easing conditions it’s the fattest pitch you get

Leads me to believe two things: 

1. If you get a 8-10% drop from here on BTC into early Dec that is fully pricing the dollar liquidity tightening and would be quite literally the cheapest BTC has been relative to its own vol adjusted trend  ever = max bid and walk away and 2. If the bottom is already in at 62 we very likely chop and consolidate whilst we wait for conditions at the margin to peak and turn 

Worth watching spreads and obviously the dollar very closely here

I think AI is one of the few industries where investors celebrate deteriorating supply conditions.

MLCC lead times are extending per new Trendforce data… now “very tight” at 40W.

Content per system keeps going up as well (eg. $AMD using +632% more of a part for MI450 boards).

Yet suppliers from Murata to Samsung Electro-Mechanics are getting sold off to oblivion.

I will continue to make the argument that we can continue to see demand acceleration in certain bottlenecks…

Despite potential overall capex reductions past 2027. Would not conflate the two like what markets are pricing in now.

It appears we are still in a late stage bear cycle with depression now creeping in. Think this is evident from broader market psychology and also paying attention to my personnel psychology.

Despite clear objective breaks in bearish market structure and positive shifts in relevant trending indicators we retraced that full move and now sit at the moment where we were over summer.

Some thoughts on the market as I believe de-risking is being driven by wider market uncertainty and what I will be watching for in the coming months:

[1] The U.S. conflict with Iran sparked a global energy crisis which has been a clear inflationary pressure and now driving FED policy. Despite oil now flowing through the strait again and an aggressive sell off in oil remains one of the key points for uncertainty.

[2] The FED has now entered into a new hiking cycle which naturally contracts global liquidity as capital flows out of risk into treasuries. Bitcoin largely benefits from a positive liquidity environment and this was the main dilemma between price action and the macro backdrop.

[3] High profile IPOs like Anthropic are multiple times oversubscribed which may be acting as a liquidity sink in the interim. Driving a rotation out of BTC into new high profile tech names. UPnL from the private markets will end up being friction on the indicies over 2027.

[4] AI related advancements as it relates to cybersecurity threats and potential weaknesses in encryption are also effecting participant psychology. I think the latter is over indexed on and the former remains a very real threat. Ultimately does not instil confidence and acts as a psychological drag.

[5] Core AI equities have seen an aggressive selloff as fears arise on revenue generated from the AI build out may not meet the debt incurred from aggressive CapEx. We has Jensen outed and concerns as it relates to open source self hosted models driving more demand from token spend. Weakness perceived in frontier labs which are set to IPO.

[6] Democrats won the mid terms and uncertainty surrounding how aggressive they will be as it relates to digital asset regulatory treatment. CFTC and SEC remains incredibly positive as it relates to on shoring digital asset innovation and market leaders.

Ultimately I think there is uncertainty from numerous vectors. Price is now indicative of a depression like market environment as it relates to where we sit on the cycle. I think rates peaking will be very important as it relates to expressing positive outlook on market liquidity. Equities are still a clear friction point for any risk on behaviour in the interim.

Going against ones own psychology and wider market psychology that depression is the latest stage of a bear market cycle. In the coming months it will most likely be wise to swim against this psychology.

Lighter is fine. It is annoying to see my funds technically stuck, but we are long past the permissionless DeFi stage, and this is the right thing to do. 

There is something like this every day. The contraction of onchain is sadly going to continue for a while as a result. People will rationally continue to remove funds the more they see high profile names getting scares.  

Once upon a time I had big chunks of my net worth in DeFi, but that hasn't been the case since 2025 now due to the increased number of risks.

I am now forced to manage the risk of how much to leave on perps dexs. 

I think once the industry demonstrates a big year on year decrease in funds lost to hackers then we will grow again. This year we have managed to lose more in hacks than onchain revenue, which is clearly insane. 

Or we somehow solve the insurance problem, which seems impossible.

Would argue that we’ve had plenty of sharp corrections since 2022 — they’ve just been much faster and v-bottomed — and the underlying conditions  are still not there for a 2022-esque bear market 

Liquidity has tightened at the margins but is still loose at the composite level, inflation impulses are actually contracting and growth is the puzzle piece here (if it does not crater we are absolutely fine for equities imo)

V hard to get a protracted bear in equities without a combination of rising inflation impulses (not headline prints) + contracting growth impulses + contracting liquidity momentum 

And people can talk about energy prices but Oil + Commodities 3m-12m ROC is negative and DXY is positive — that is unequivocally a disinflationary force — too much focus on absolute levels and little focus on momentum

Would definitely say the case for that weaker combination of macro impulses is stronger than it has been for a while but it’s still not there concretely 

I think the signature of Trump regimes is sharp and sporadic corrections into vol panics and v-reversals - I don’t see this changing in 2027 as it stands 

But obviously if my macro modelling starts screaming this time is actually different I will share here — not seeing anything outside of normal corrections and chop atm 

Crypto is a v different beast and extremely reliant on liquidity conditions particularly, so remains to be seen what happens there going into 2027 — but yeah what was turning into a tailwind from a dollar liquidity POV has very quickly materialised into a headwind

Morgan Stanley sends a note to clients using the term:

“Max Overweight” for global equities.

Arguing that AI capex cycle remains intact and sustains corporate earnings into 2027.

They told clients:

- hold less cash, trim commodities and exposure to bonds
- move Europe/Japanese equities to overweight
- Global stocks trade ~15x fwd earnings (MSCI ACWI), the cheapest since 2023
- AI theme is expected to spread beyond the hyperscalers
- Global earnings growth is forecast at 13% in 2027 and 8% in 2028

But flagged:

- Inflation could force more tightening than the two further Fed hikes
- AI capex cycle may not last as long as assumed

Earlier this week they argued:

“The hedge fund deleveraging unwind has been brutal since October.

While retail investors remain calm and long-term oriented, levered institutional hedge funds have acted as ‘chickens with their heads chopped off’ (IMO), 

moving daily stock prices around at nonsensical speeds.”

Anyway the most recent time I found this term used was 14 years ago June 8th, 2012.

Where they called “maximum” overweight on emerging-market equities.

Usually I treat this as noise but TIL “max overweight” was a term used.

tweets.text:
What would happen to $NVDA earnings multiple if investors could sleep well?

We can learn a little bit by looking at what’s happened with $AAPL’s multiple over the past 15 years. Setting aside all of the near-term transition risk. 

During the iPhone’s hypergrowth phase from 2009 to 2011, AAPL’s earnings multiple expanded dramatically. But as growth began to slow, investors believed those hypergrowth days were behind it and the most attractive part of the story was over. As a result, AAPL’s multiple compressed to roughly 12x forward earnings in 2012.

What investors missed was that hardware can become a business with annuity characteristics if a company maintains a sustainable edge. Despite a brutal smartphone market, Apple showed it could maintain pricing power, retain customers, and generate recurring revenue through predictable hardware upgrades.

Eventually, investors realized Apple didn’t need iPhone growth above 20% to be exceptional. Steady sleep well at night revenue growth of 5 to 10% and earnings growth of 10 to 15% proved hugely valuable, helping the multiple climb from roughly 12 times in 2012 to about 34x calendar 2027 earnings today.

Back to NVDA. The question isn’t just how long the current boom lasts, but whether the company can prove durable pricing power and a recurring upgrade cycle for its GPUs.

Those massive data centers being built today will need upgrading starting  in five years. If Nvidia keeps its edge and captures those upgrades, even with 10 to 15% earnings growth, you can make a case for a higher multiple.

The lesson from Apple is that valuation multiples don’t always peak when growth does. Sometimes the biggest expansion comes when investors can sleep well at night given durability and predictability become clear.

tweets.text:
This is one of the most frustrating videos I’ve ever seen of two people speaking past each other. And the main issue is they’re both right

Anyone can become wealthy, but everyone definitely can’t

O’Leary is giving the guy sound advice - work smarter, and more pragmatically toward your goals, rather than just harder to stay where you are. But whilst everything O’Leary suggests is a requirement for success, it’s far from a guarantee, and the current environment only stacks the odds further against people

The reaction of the security guard honestly makes me want to scream at him, for how dismissive he is of any ambition he could show and the conviction with which he describes his own defeatist situation. And yet, I understand it. The social contract we were promised when we were younger - study, work hard, get a job and you’ll have a decent standard of living - is getting harder and harder for the average person to hold onto

And O’Leary’s advice is incredibly generic in the face of that. It’s individual advice, ignoring a structural problem. If this guy does rise above and succeed, it doesn’t mean O’Leary has nobody left to debate. He’d just be sat across from another security guard, with the same 80-hour work week. Anyone can become wealthy, but everyone can’t

What people’s acceptance of their circumstances is really saying is that they did what they were told, and it hasn’t worked out the way it was meant to. And whilst their frustration may sound like entitlement, I think if we are to demand more of the individual, we should also demand more of our society to support that ambition, before it’s crushed and they become victims of their circumstances. The truth is - nobody’s owed anything, but we should still expect our society to offer a lot more than this

So yes, listen to the billionaire. Just don’t expect him to be listening back

Over the past few weeks I've gone from thinking leanPCS is total bull to being a total bull. So let me explain some of these buzzwords in more detail.

At the core, 8288 is about hyper-scaling data and execution for any computation that needs to get performed on a piece of data once, the chain learns the answer, and then we never need to see that data again. This sounds very specific, but it includes most "heavy" things happening on Ethereum:

* Signatures
* STARKs
* Merkle branches
* FHE computation
* ...

Really the first two are the most important.

Once we go quantum-safe, signatures get bigger (65 bytes ECDSA -> 1-6 kB WOTS/SPHINCS depending on params) and ZKPs get much bigger (200-1000 bytes with groth16, PLONK, etc -> 128 kB with STARKs). This is unsustainable to put on chain, and 8288 fixes this.

8288 works by aggregating STARKs in the mempool. First, you as a user generate the STARK or SPHINCS signature or PCS opening (more on that last one later), and publish it. Then, each node listens. Each tick, each node takes all of the new objects that it has seen, and generates a STARK containing a list of "claims":

"pubkey P has signed message M"
"program X run on data D has output Y"
"p(X) = Y for some polynomial P whose hash is H"

and a proof that it has seen a signature, STARK or PCS opening verifying those claims. So the only information getting re-broadcasted is:

(i) hashes of inputs and outputs (~64-96 bytes per claim)
(ii) a single STARK proof per tick

These aggregate proofs themselves get re-aggregated, and eventually you get to a single "master proof" in the block, that verifies that all of those statements are true. And so the only other data that has to actually go on chain is the statements (the (P, M), (X, D, Y), (X, Y, H) tuples I described above), not the actual signatures or proofs. This gets put into a specialized frame type.

Now, let's get into the leanSPHINCS vs leanSTARK vs leanPCS part.

The core distinction is: *what is the underlying object that the user is creating?*

In leanSPHINCS, it's a signature, and specifically this particular type of purely-hash-based signature: https://t.co/HOazliHq9N

If we add leanSPHINCS, then users will be able to make quantum-safe accounts, and pay only a little bit of gas (4096 for the 64 bytes) for each signature. So we get scalable quantum-safety for regular accounts, multisigs, etc. But it's only one specific signature scheme, you can't do anything else.

In leanSTARK, it's a STARK. This means it's fully general: the user runs whatever computation they want, and publish a STARK of it. So you can use it for:

* Any signature scheme (including eg. lattice-based ones if you like those)
* A multisig that hides its internal logic
* Privacy protocols
* Private account abstraction: authorization logic that depends on some value hidden elsewhere in the state, so you can have one key that controls all your accounts without publicly linking them to each other

Basically, it's a free for all, in the same way the EVM is a free for all.

But leanSTARK has a practical downside. The protocol would have to specify the language in which users write their programs (we call this the "ISA"). So we would have to agree on that language. This is a really big deal - it's the first big case of "Ethereum moving beyond the EVM" - and so it's likely to take time to agree on the details of it, especially since the ISA would be hard to upgrade. There are benefits to taking longer on this, figuring out the ideal ISA, and then even giving access to it inside regular contracts.

LeanPCS is the third option. PCS stands for "polynomial commitment scheme": a proof that P(x) = y. The most important thing to know about PCSes is that they are by far the most important "hard" component of a STARK (see here: https://t.co/EEQWMU0gAf ). If you have a "magic PCS oracle" (which from the EVM's point of view, 8288 is), you can verify a STARK in ~20-40k gas.

The most important gain with PCS is that there is far less that we need to choose. Specifying a PCS only requires specifying a field, and there is a natural option: the 128 bit binary field (technically, we can go more general than that, and say the 2^k-bit binary recursive tower field, going up to 256)

LeanPCS is less efficient than leanSTARK onchain, because you would have to put multiple claims to prove one thing. But it's arguably more efficient offchain, because you have much more flexibility to choose proof systems.

But most importantly, leanPCS gives you the same generality as leanSTARK, in a way that could potentially be implemented very quickly. And once we figure out the ISA, we can add leanSTARK later.

So there is a route to getting "the cryptographic proof singularity" much faster than any of us expected, and that route runs through 8288 with leanPCS.
 https://t.co/dUHONMh75g

But leanSTARK has a practical downside. The protocol would have to specify the language in which users write their programs (we call this the "ISA"). So we would have to agree on that language. This is a really big deal - it's the first big case of "Ethereum moving beyond the EVM" - and so it's likely to take time to agree on the details of it, especially since the ISA would be hard to upgrade. There are benefits to taking longer on this, figuring out the ideal ISA, and then even giving access to it inside regular contracts.

LeanPCS is the third option. PCS stands for "polynomial commitment scheme": a proof that P(x) = y. The most important thing to know about PCSes is that they are by far the most important "hard" component of a STARK (see here: https://t.co/EEQWMU0gAf ). If you have a "magic PCS oracle" (which from the EVM's point of view, 8288 is), you can verify a STARK in ~20-40k gas.

The most important gain with PCS is that there is far less that we need to choose. Specifying a PCS only requires specifying a field, and there is a natural option: the 128 bit binary field (technically, we can go more general than that, and say the 2^k-bit binary recursive tower field, going up to 256)

LeanPCS is less efficient than leanSTARK onchain, because you would have to put multiple claims to prove one thing. But it's arguably more efficient offchain, because you have much more flexibility to choose proof systems.

But most importantly, leanPCS gives you the same generality as leanSTARK, in a way that could potentially be implemented very quickly. And once we figure out the ISA, we can add leanSTARK later.

So there is a route to getting "the cryptographic proof singularity" much faster than any of us expected, and that route runs through 8288 with leanPCS.

Bitcoin is a volatile asset, which means taking the lumps. Here are my thoughts on the game of chicken that is investing in the accelerating debt-debasement era.

Last week's fall was a 3.4 sigma vol-adjusted move, #21 of 299 since 2014.

In August, I said the breakout was unlikely to fail. But it always happened against a late liquidity-cycle setup, where debt growth > liquidity growth.

What matters now is where the fall happened and how liquidity drivers move.

Above my market regime filter, falls like this were higher 6 months later 8 of 9 times. Below it, where we are now, 10 of 17 (median +2%). Statistically, the skew is to the downside. 

But it's the same message as February's capitulation near $60K: this is a value zone. Boring as it sounds, idle capital should see this as an opportunity. Another leg down, if it comes, would be a gift; key levels are realised price and long-term holder cost at around ~$53k & ~$48k, respectively. These levels aren't FUD; there is an air pocket below $60k based on onchain cost levels. 

On-chain, this looks more like a shakeout than capitulation. Recent buyers are selling at a loss but long-term holders aren't (LTH-SOPR ~1.0 vs 0.4-0.7 at cycle lows), and 30-day realised losses are a tenth of February's.

Flipside, a weekly close above ~$73K reclaims my trend-regime filter, and ~$75k reclaims short-term holder cost basis. That's only 15% above here and within the bounds of pure noise. The point is that price is wedged tight between key levels. 

The trigger is the macro drivers turning. They're going the wrong way but could be near exhaustion. I say near, but nothing is definitive until the DXY reverses. $BTC inflections are typically signalled by dollar reversals. 

My expectation is the definitive liquidity low in 2027. Bitcoin should bottom before it. Unless it's completely delinked from global liquidity (it's at its lowest in the modern era), which I do not believe; the August Bessent buyback announcement is a good indication: when liquidity turns, Bitcoin will outperform every other asset.

I suspect 2027 is when they will be forced to swerve again. Every regime is different; liquidity mechanisms morph out of necessity. We are late stage in the global debt & debasement game. And owning Bitcoin is always a game of chicken with the central planners.

The $NVDA news just keeps getting worse.

- Entire administration is turning on him. Rubio likely leaked the initial reports and Bessent went on Fox yesterday and demanded a new CEO and answers from the Nvidia board.

- New investigation today found empty server racks in Indonesia from Megaspeed. An affair could be forgiven, selling to China is going to be harder for the market to forgive if it was intentional. 

- Semianalysis just cut their 2028 capex forecast by 28%, indicating that capex growth has peaked. This really hurts NVDA.

- Jensen now has to deal with multiple investigations and the company, going into earnings, might say anything that gets interpreted as bearish when it comes to guidance/growth/margins even if it is slightly off from expectations.

- If the new CEO is going to cut most of the circular financing that Jensen did, may not be as easy for them to hit numbers when some of these smaller AI companies don’t have the funding to buy their chips. 

I know people are saying that the valuation has discounted all of this from $240, sure, but if this stock isn’t trading on valuation and more on sentiment, if the sentiment becomes that it’s just too hard to own…thats where you get the ugliness continuing.

Just becoming harder to measure the risks that are piling up.
